reconcile.note: Fausset and his co-commentators read Matthew's mountain scene as a supernaturally extended vision rather than a literal panorama, so no particular earth-shape is presupposed.

discrepancy.note: Strauss argues the panoramic mountain of Matthew 4:8 only makes sense on the ancient flat-earth model, not a spherical globe.

quotes.text: No answer remains but that such a mountain existed only in the ancient idea of the earth as a plain, and in the popular imagination, which can easily stretch a mountain up to heaven, and sharpen an eye to penetrate infinity.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), trans. George Eliot, on Matthew 4:8.

sides.snippet: he who sits above the circle of the earth
sides.verseText: [It is] he who sits above the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants of it are as grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens as a curtain, and spreads them out as a tent to dwell in;

sides.snippet: showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
sides.verseText: Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
